entries.name: Gameplay mechanics
entries.description:
Baldur's Gate 3 is a turn-based adventure with a wide variety of gameplay mechanics. Understanding the core mechanics can help the players navigate the challenging world of Baldurs Gate 3. 
This page will give a general overview over the most important aspects, to understand certain nuances, reading linked articles might be required. 
Every section has a dedicated wiki page with further information.

entries.name: Turn-based mode
entries.description:
Turn-based mode is one of the two gameplay modes in Baldur's Gate 3, in which time passes in turns and rounds, as opposed to real-time mode, where events occur in real-time. Story events and cutscenes could be considered a third gameplay mode, in which nether turn-based nor real-time action are possible; it could also be considered not a mode at all, but outside of normal gameplay. 
Each round, the game cycles through each participating creature's turn, during which each creature may move or take actions. One round passes when all creatures complete their turn.

entries.name: Actions
entries.description:
Actions are the acts taken by creatures on their turns in Baldur's Gate 3. Actions are generally taken to deal damage or inflict harmful conditions, but can also be taken to heal or aid allies.
A special form of action – known as a reaction – can be used as a response to certain triggers, including on the turns of other creatures.
Taking actions usually requires the acting creature to expend one of three resources:

entries.name: Initiative
entries.description: Initiative determines the order of turns during combat.

entries.name: Reactions
entries.description:
Reactions are actions taken in response to a trigger, and can be taken even if triggered on another creature's turn.
Some reactions require the acting creature to expend a  Reaction resource, whereas other reactions do not. Those that do not are generally class features which use the reaction system, such as  Divine Smite,  Reckless Attack, or  Sneak Attack.

entries.name: Resources
entries.description:
Resources are expendable units in Baldur's Gate 3 that determine what a creature is able to do at any given time, as well as how long they must wait before they are able to do it again.
Depleted resources must recharge in order for them to be used again. Resources always recharge on taking a long rest, but some also recharge on taking a short rest, or at the beginning of the creature's turn.
A resource that recharges at the start of the turn, when used outside turn-based mode or combat, will recharge almost immediately after use. However, if used to initiate or enter combat, it does not recharge at the start of the user's turn.
All creatures have a set of common resources available to them, and most other resources are gained along with the actions or features that use them.

entries.name: Dice rolls
entries.description: Dice rolls are a central game mechanic in Baldur's Gate 3. When the player character attempts most actions, a roll helps resolve the outcome based on the relevant DC or AC and any modifiers for the acting character. Player choices decide the approach, while a roll determines the end result, such as whether an ability check succeeds, an attack hits, or how much damage is dealt.

entries.name: Abilities
entries.description:
Abilities are representations of a creature's physical and mental attributes in Baldur's Gate 3. There are six abilities in Baldur's Gate 3, and every creature has a set of six ability scores – numerical values which represent how well they perform at each ability.
Each ability score translates directly into an ability score modifier – modifiers which function as bonuses or penalties that are added to most dice rolls in the game.

entries.name: Advantage
entries.description: Advantage and  Disadvantage are terms used for two different gameplay mechanics that can greatly affect the success of dice rolls. First they are used for rolling two dice, second they are used for contesting ability checks.

entries.name: Attacks
entries.description:
Attacks are attempts by a creature at hitting a target, usually with a weapon or a spell.
The outcome of an attempted attack is determined by the attacker making an attack roll against the target's AC. If the attempt is successful, the attack may deal damage and / or inflict a condition.
Attacks can be made by taking an Attack action, as well by taking any action that requires the attacker to make an attack roll.
Spell attacks are attack rolls made as part of casting a spell.

entries.name: Concentration
entries.description: Concentration is a game mechanic used in spellcasting. Spells with the  Concentration tag require the caster to continuously focus on them in order to maintain their effects.

entries.name: Damage
entries.description:
Damage is a number which represents how deadly a threat is. When a creature takes damage, their current hit point total is reduced by the amount specified.
Damage is dealt with attacks and other harmful actions, as well as by a variety of conditions.

entries.name: Critical hit
entries.description:
Critical hits occur when an attacker rolls a natural 20 on their attack roll. Critical hits automatically land regardless of the target's armour class, and the attacker also rolls twice the normal number of dice to determine damage dealt.
While initially a stochastic game mechanic, a number of features, abilities, and items allow one to manipulate the odds of scoring a critical hit. Combined with effects that make critical hits themselves stronger, building around critical hits can be a valid strategic option.

entries.name: Damage mechanics
entries.description: A single attack, spell, trap, or other harmful effect can often result in multiple Damage Rolls. Determining the resulting damage from these various rolls can be difficult due to hidden mechanics which are commonly referred to by the community as damage "sources" and damage "riders". The term damage "instances" is sometimes used in place of damage "sources," but for the purpose of this page the only terms to be used are damage source(s) and damage rider(s). The game does not inform players what is a damage source vs. what is a damage rider, or how these two interact with each other. This page describes the mechanical differences between damage sources and damage riders, how they interact, and lists which effects and abilities fall into each category.

entries.name: Healing
entries.description:
Healing is the process of restoring lost  hit points to a creature.
Healing can never restore more hit points than a creature's hit point maximum, and cannot restore temporary hit points. Player characters are generally only able to heal their party members and allies, not hostile or neutral creatures.
Most healing effects use a dice roll, similar to a damage roll, to determine how many hit points are restored; for example  Cure Wounds cast as a level 1 spell 1d8⁠⁠Hit Points plus the caster's spellcasting modifier as a flat bonus. More rarely, an effect may heal a fixed amount, like the  Heal spell.
Any amount of healing removes the  Downed or  Bleeding conditions, and many sources of healing also have other beneficial effects; for example healing potions also remove the  Burning condition when drunk, and some healing spells also remove diseases.

entries.name: Inspiration
entries.description: Inspiration is a game mechanic in Baldur's Gate 3. Inspiration points can be spent to re-roll certain failed d20 rolls, and are earned by making choices which fit the player character's background. Inspirations are shared between all party members.

entries.name: Saving throws
entries.description: Saving throws are automatic dice rolls representing a creature’s attempt to “save” themselves from harm. They are provoked by spells, the hostile actions (other than attacks) of other creatures, or hazards like traps and surfaces. Saves are always associated with a specific ability (except for death saving throws), and are always rolled against a target Difficulty Class (DC), both determined by the triggering effect. When successful, they reduce or prevent harmful effects.

entries.name: Alchemy
entries.description: Alchemy is a crafting mechanic that allows to turn your collection of herbs, wild mushrooms, crystals, and monster components into potions, elixirs, grenades, and coatings. All alchemical ingredients including extracts of them are stored in the Alchemy Pouch.

entries.name: Approval
entries.description:
In Baldur's Gate 3, every companion has an approval rating towards the player character. Approval or disapproval is gained based on certain choices made in dialogue, quests, combat, etc.
This system plays a pivotal role in each character's personal quest and how they react to the player character's actions; certain outcomes can only occur if the companion has high enough approval with the player character. 
Dialogue with companions changes based on their current approval rating with the player character, and might also affect the Difficulty Class required to persuade them. Companions also have different thresholds required in order to begin or continue a romance with them.

entries.name: Dialogue
entries.description: Dialogue in Baldur's Gate 3 occurs overhead when travelling and when interacting with certain characters.

entries.name: Romance
entries.description: Romance is an optional feature in Baldur's Gate 3. The player character can pursue romantic relationships with several companions, ranging from brief flings to long-term commitments. They can also engage in separate trysts with other non-companion characters throughout the game.

entries.name: Tags
entries.description: Tags in Baldur's Gate 3 are identifiers attached to creatures. They can have various effects on gameplay, like enabling additional dialogue options, or deciding whether the creature can be targeted by certain spells. There are many different tags throughout the game. Some are defined by a character's background and inherent traits, while others are obtained by performing certain actions.

entries.name: Traders
entries.description: Traders are characters who have an expanded set of items and extra money. They are marked with a  on the minimap. Talking to a trader often leads to a dialogue option which opens the trading interface, Some traders have no role in the game beyond their trade inventory.

entries.name: Trading and item pricing
entries.description:
Trading is a central gameplay mechanic in Baldur's Gate 3 revolving around the sale and barter of Items and Gold. Depending on which Character is talking to a given Trader, including the trader's Attitude to the character, the character's Persuasion value, and the Difficulty setting of the game, a trade price multiplier is calculated. This multiplier is then applied to each item's inherent value, giving the prices for the character.
The price modifier is calculated as:

entries.name: Attitude
entries.description: Attitude is used to determine the favourability (or lack thereof) of otherwise non-aggressive Non-Player Characters and the prices they accept when trading. Attacking a character, stealing, or interacting with objects without permission may cause a nearby character who can be traded with (i.e. merchant or trader) to lose attitude towards the offending character. The only way to increase attitude is to gift gold or items of value.

entries.name: Campsite
entries.description: The Campsite is a region in  Baldur's Gate 3. It is a special location the party discovers when their first Long Rest is initiated, and can subsequently be travelled to via the right menu, long resting or fast travel.

entries.name: Camp Events
entries.description: Camp Events are story related events that happen at the Campsite in Baldur's Gate 3. Below is a list of camp events and their requirements.

entries.name: Magic Mirror
entries.description: The Magic Mirror is an environmental object in the Campsite which can be used to change the appearance of a Custom or Dark Urge player character, or a hireling, but not other origin characters.

entries.name: Resting
entries.description: Resting is a gameplay mechanic used to restore lost hit points and depleted resources.

entries.name: Environment
entries.description:
The Environment of Baldur's Gate 3 as defined here encompasses physical battlefield conditions that influence movement, visibility, positioning, and combat outcomes. It is a 
summation for gameplay mechanics mentioned in the navbar.

entries.name: Clouds
entries.description: Clouds are a type of area. Clouds hang directly above the ground, as opposed to surfaces that coat the ground itself.

entries.name: Darkvision mechanics
entries.description: Darkvision is a passive feature that changes how natural darkness affects a creature. The related passive feature  Superior Darkvision is equivalent, just with a longer effective range. There are also some other passive features with a similar or equivalent effect. This page explains some details pertaining to such features and the related gameplay mechanics.

entries.name: Difficult Terrain
entries.description:
Difficult Terrain halves the Movement Speed of creatures moving through it, requiring 2 m (7 ft) of movement to move 1 m (3 ft) through this type of area.
Examples of difficult terrain include:

entries.name: High ground rules
entries.description: High ground is an important mechanic in Baldur's Gate 3 combat. Holding high ground over enemies grants a number of benefits including increased range and attack roll bonuses.

entries.name: Obscurity
entries.description:
Obscurity defines the visibility of creatures and objects based on environmental lighting and magical effects. A location is categorized as a Clear Area, Lightly Obscured, or Heavily Obscured depending on factors like ambient light, shadows, or spells which create areas such as  Fog,  Darkness, and  Cloudkill. For example, in many cases the obscurity of an area can be increased – going from clear area to lightly obscured – by snuffing out a light source such as a candle. While a creature is simply standing in these areas, they are 'obscured' by the environment, but they only gain the specific  Clear Area,  Lightly Obscured, or  Heavily Obscured status conditions if they successfully use the  Hide action.
It is important to distinguish between the environmental state of an area and the status condition of a creature. Many pieces of equipment grant bonuses – such as increased Critical Hit chances or damage resistances – whenever the wearer is 'obscured.' Unless the item's description specifically requires the user to be Hiding, these benefits apply as long as the character is standing in a Lightly or Heavily Obscured space. If an item does not specify a level of obscurity, both Lightly and Heavily Obscured environments will trigger its effects.
Environmental obscurity is the primary factor in determining whether a hidden character is detected within an enemy's line of sight. A character attempting to hide in a Clear Area is spotted instantly. In a Lightly Obscured area, the character must succeed on a Stealth Check against the enemy's Passive Perception to remain unseen. A Heavily Obscured area generally makes a character impossible to detect by sight alone. However, creatures with  Darkvision effectively reduce the obscurity level by one step: they automatically spot characters in Lightly Obscured areas and force those in Heavily Obscured areas to roll Stealth checks. Regardless of the environment, a character who is not actively hiding receives no protection from line-of-sight detection.

entries.name: Sight mechanics
entries.description: Sight or Vision in Baldur's Gate 3 is governed by a combination of physical lines of sight, environmental lighting (obscurity), and specific surface/area properties. These interacting systems dictate whether a creature can be targeted, whether an attack receives a bonus or a penalty, and whether a character can successfully hide.

entries.name: Surfaces
entries.description: Surfaces are a type of area.

entries.name: Trap
entries.description: A trap is an environmental hazard which causes sudden unwanted conditions and / or damage when triggered.

entries.name: Items
entries.description: There are different types of items in the game. Items can be of different rarities which are: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very rare, Legendary, and Story Item.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.description:
Equipment are important items for use in the game. They include weapons that deal damage to enemies, and armour for protection from them. They can also give useful bonuses to characters such as extra spells, special enchantments, and so on.
The reader can find detailed description for each type of equipment below.

entries.name: Amulets
entries.description: Amulets are equippable accessories which provide beneficial passives or allow characters to cast certain Spells.

entries.name: Armour
entries.description: Armour is a type of equipment that provides bonuses to the wearer's Armour Class (AC), decreasing their chance of being hit by attacks.

entries.name: Cloaks
entries.description: Cloaks are equippable accessories. At uncommon or higher rarities, they may provide Passive features, bonuses to Skills, or the ability to cast certain Spells.

entries.name: Clothing
entries.description:
Clothing is a form of Equipment that provides no additional protection against damage, but allows classes with no armour proficiency (like Sorcerer and Wizard) to cast Spells in combat.
When wearing clothing, your Armour Class is equal to 10 plus your Dexterity Modifier. Also, since it is not classified as armour, all the spells and equipment with the condition "While you are not wearing any armour" such as Mage Armour still fully function while wearing them.

entries.name: Footwear
entries.description: Footwear includes boots of various types.  They can provide bonuses to saving throws, or grant item-specific actions such as the ability to cast a certain spell.

entries.name: Handwear
entries.description: Handwear includes gloves, gauntlets, bracers, and so on.  They can provide bonuses to saving throws, or grant item-specific actions such as the ability to cast a certain spell.

entries.name: Headwear
entries.description: Headwear includes caps, helmets, circlets, and other items worn in the Helmet slot. They can protect the wearer from Critical Hits, provide bonuses to Saving Throws, or grant item-specific actions such as the ability to cast a certain spell.

entries.name: Light Sources
entries.description:
Light Sources are simple melee weapons wielded in one hand, which can be added to the "Light Source" equipment slot. Once added, they can be equipped to the main hand with a hotkey to shine light in the area surrounding that character. The previously equipped weapon will be unequipped until the hotkey is pressed again or it is manually re-equipped, which requires an Action.
Light Sources can also be manually equipped in the off-hand slot, but only if a Light Weapon is in the main hand (unless the character has the Dual Wielder Feat).
In combat, they can be used as improvised Clubs which deal extra damage when lit.
Unlike other equipment slots which provide bonuses for each equipped item, objects in the Light Source slot are not 'active' until moved to a hand slot, meaning they do not illuminate the area unless being carried in either hand. The only partial exception to this is the  Moonlantern, which provides its protection when in the Light Source slot, but still does not illuminate the area while there.

entries.name: Musical Instruments
entries.description: Musical instruments can be equipped and used with the Perform action. Bard characters will also use their instruments when casting spells.

entries.name: Rings
entries.description: Rings are equippable accessories. At uncommon or higher rarities, they may provide passive features, bonuses to skills, or the ability to cast certain spells.

entries.name: Weapons
entries.description: Weapons are a type of equipment used in attacks that deal damage. Weapons also give proficient wielders access to special weapon actions, and are a useful tool for any adventurer.

entries.name: Arrows
entries.description:
Arrows are Consumables that are fired from ranged weapons to deal extra damage, create Surfaces, inflict Conditions or produce other effects.
Arrows can be looted as well as bought from vendors, but they cannot be crafted.

entries.name: Coatings
entries.description:
Coatings are Consumables that can apply a variety of effects to equipped weapons that aid in combat for a short period of time. Some coatings apply poisons to deal extra damage, while others improve hit chance, apply Conditions, or impose Disadvantage on the target. 
Coatings can be looted, bought from vendors, or crafted with the Alchemy system.

entries.name: Elixirs
entries.description:
Elixirs are consumable items which can be consumed as a bonus action to apply a variety of beneficial effects, similar to potions. Unlike potions, the effects of an elixir last until either taking a long rest or drinking another elixir. Many elixirs can be created with Alchemy.
A character can only benefit from the effects of one elixir at a time: in most cases, drinking an elixir immediately cancels any active effects of one previously consumed.
Other activities can cause elixir benefits to end, such as praying at the altar to  Shar in the Gauntlet of Shar.

entries.name: Grenades
entries.description: Grenades are Consumables which can be  Thrown to deal Damage, inflict Conditions, create Surfaces, Knock back creatures, or produce other effects. Most Coatings, Elixirs, and Potions can also act as Grenades when thrown. Many grenades also can explode.

entries.name: Potions
entries.description:
Potions are Consumables that can restore Hit Points, cure Conditions, or to grant a variety of other effects when consumed (or, in some cases, applied after being thrown). These effects can range from gaining extra actions in combat, speaking to animals, or even gaining the benefit of Long Rest without resting.
Potions can be looted, bought from vendors, or crafted with the Alchemy system.

entries.name: Scrolls
entries.description: Scrolls are magical Consumables that allow characters to cast spells without expending spell slots or having a spellcasting class. Scrolls can be very useful in situations when you do not have any remaining spell slots, when you need to cast a spell you do not have prepared, or when you do not have the required spellcaster in the party.

entries.name: Containers
entries.description:
Containers are items that can be interacted with either in the world or from inside a character's inventory to store and retrieve items.
Unless otherwise noted, containers can be picked up, moved and destroyed by most any creature.

entries.name: Miscellaneous
entries.description: Miscellaneous are various items which can be collected during the party's journey.

entries.name: Creatures
entries.description: Creatures are all living entities in Baldur's Gate 3. All characters, animals and monsters are creatures.

entries.name: Charisma
entries.description:
Charisma is an ability score and the primary ability of Bards, Warlocks, and Sorcerers. Charisma affects its related skills (Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion) and improves spellcasting for Bards, Paladins, Warlocks and Sorcerers (better chance to hit enemies with spell attack rolls; increases the Difficulty Class of spells with saving throws).
Increasing one's Charisma Modifier also improves the prices offered by Traders (by increasing the Persuasion skill bonus).

entries.name: Constitution
entries.description:
Constitution is an ability score. Constitution affects your maximum hit points and concentration saving throws.
Your Constitution modifier is added to the number of hit points gained per level (including negative values), and is applied retroactively.

entries.name: Dexterity
entries.description:
Dexterity is an ability score and a key ability of Rogues, Rangers, Monks, and other wielders of finesse weapons.
Dexterity affects your Acrobatics, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth skills, as well as your attack rolls for ranged weapons and finesse weapons. It also affects your Initiative and Armour Class.

entries.name: Intelligence
entries.description:
Intelligence is an ability score and the primary ability of wizards.
Intelligence affects your Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, and Religion skills. It also improves spellcasting for wizards, fighters (useful for Eldritch Knights), and rogues (useful for Arcane Tricksters), by increasing the chance of hitting an enemy with spell attack rolls, due to the increased Difficulty Class of spells with saving throws. In addition, it increases the maximum number of prepared spells for wizards.

entries.name: Strength
entries.description:
Strength is an ability score and the primary ability of Barbarian, Fighter, Paladin.
Strength affects your Athletics skill and attack rolls so you become better at melee combat. It also determines how far you can jump, how much you can carry and how far you can shove (possibly based on Athletics).

entries.name: Wisdom
entries.description:
Wisdom is an ability score, and the primary ability of Clerics and Druids.
Wisdom affects your Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Perception, and Survival skills and improves spellcasting for Clerics, Druids, Monks and Rangers (better chance to hit enemies with spell attack rolls; increases the Difficulty Class of spells with Saving Throws).

entries.name: Acrobatics
entries.description:
Acrobatics is a Dexterity-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Dexterity Score, the more likely they will succeed on Acrobatics Checks, including resisting being shoved.

entries.name: Animal Handling
entries.description:
Animal Handling is a Wisdom-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Wisdom Score, the more likely they will succeed on Animal Handling Checks to deal with animals.

entries.name: Arcana
entries.description:
Arcana is an Intelligence-based skill.
It represents an academic understanding of arcane magic and the Weave, but it is not required to cast spells. The higher a creature's Intelligence Score, the more likely they will succeed on Arcana Checks.

entries.name: Athletics
entries.description:
Athletics is a Strength-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Strength Score, the more likely they will succeed Athletics Checks, including resisting being shoved.

entries.name: Deception
entries.description:
Deception is a Charisma-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Charisma Score, the more likely they will succeed on Deception Checks to mislead others in conversations.

entries.name: History
entries.description:
History is an Intelligence-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Intelligence Score, the more likely they will succeed on History Checks to recall history on a particular topic.

entries.name: Insight
entries.description:
Insight is a Wisdom-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Wisdom Score, the more likely they are to succeed on Insight Checks to detect lies and read people's body language.

entries.name: Intimidation
entries.description:
Intimidation is a Charisma-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Charisma Score, the more likely they will succeed on Intimidation Checks to scare others into submission.

entries.name: Investigation
entries.description:
Investigation is an Intelligence-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Intelligence Score, the more likely they will succeed Investigation Checks to uncover hidden clues or objects.

entries.name: Medicine
entries.description:
Medicine is a Wisdom-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Wisdom Score, the more likely they will succeed on Medicine Checks to diagnose diseases or recognize illnesses.

entries.name: Nature
entries.description:
Nature is an Intelligence-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Intelligence Score, the more likely they will succeed on Nature Checks to recognize plants and natural creatures.

entries.name: Perception
entries.description:
Perception is a Wisdom-based Skill. 
The higher a creature's Wisdom Score, the more likely it will succeed on Perception Checks to spot hidden objects or creatures.

entries.name: Performance
entries.description:
Performance is a Charisma-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Charisma Score, the more likely they will succeed on Performance Checks to entertain others or imitate characters.

entries.name: Persuasion
entries.description: Persuasion is a Charisma-based skill used almost exclusively for dialogue ability checks. Persuasion also affects the prices offered by traders alongside their Attitude value towards the party member talking to them.

entries.name: Religion
entries.description:
Religion is an Intelligence-based Skill. 
The higher a creature's Intelligence Score, the more likely they will succeed on Religion Checks to recognize religious details.

entries.name: Sleight of Hand
entries.description:
Sleight of Hand  is a Dexterity-based skill. 
The higher a creature's Dexterity score, the more likely they are to succeed on Sleight of Hand ability checks to pick locks, pick pockets, and disarm traps.

entries.name: Stealth
entries.description:
Stealth is a Dexterity-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Dexterity Score, the more likely they will succeed on Stealth Checks to stay hidden from enemies or other NPCs.

entries.name: Survival
entries.description:
Survival is a Wisdom-based Skill.
The higher a creature's Wisdom Score, the more likely they will succeed on Survival Checks pertaining to hunting and the wilderness.

entries.name: Features
entries.description: Features grant a creature passive effects or allow it use certain actions.

entries.name: Conditions
entries.description: Conditions are changes in a character's status, both beneficial and harmful. They can be imposed by certain Spells, class features, surfaces and other environmental hazards, etc. Many conditions are temporary, and some can be removed with the right spell or potion.

entries.name: Feats
entries.description:
Feats are features that grant a character unique improvements. All classes select one feat at class levels 4, 8, and 12. Fighters select an additional feat at level 6; Rogues select an additional feat at level 10.
See  D&D 5e feat changes for an overview of difference between feats in 5e D&D and Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Illithid powers
entries.description: Illithid powers are special abilities tied to the mind flayer tadpole infecting the player character, their Origin companions and certain non-Origin companions.

entries.name: Passive feature
entries.description: Passive features are qualities that modify the statistics and capabilities of an entity.

entries.name: Permanent bonuses
entries.description:
Permanent bonuses are special conditions, character enhancements, or other abilities. With very rare exceptions, these bonuses remain with the character after long resting. Some but not all remain even after death.
There are many different permanent character enhancements or bonuses that can be obtained throughout Baldur's Gate 3. See below for details on these bonuses and how they can be obtained.

entries.name: Spells
entries.description:
Spells are magical effects that are created by creatures via spellcasting. Spells are frequently cast to deal damage and provide healing, or to inflict conditions on their targets.
All classes are capable of casting spells with the help of scrolls and magic items, and classes with the Spellcasting or Pact Magic features – called spellcasters – have spell slots they can expend to cast spells they know, without the need for scrolls.

entries.name: List of all spells
entries.description: This is a list of all spells in Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Armour Class
entries.description: Armour Class (AC) is a measurement of how difficult a creature is to be hit by an attack. In order to successfully hit a creature, the results of an attack roll must have a number equal to or greater than the target's Armour Class. AC can be increased by equipping armour and shields, by selecting certain feats when leveling up, or utilizing certain spells.

entries.name: List of creature types
entries.description: This page lists the various creature types found throughout Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Hit points
entries.description:
Hit points (or HP), given in numbers, represent a creature's life force, or an object's structural integrity. For creatures, they indicate how much damage can be taken before being  Downed. For items, hit points show how much damage can be taken before being destroyed.
Taking damage reduces current hit points and affects how injured a character appears, with more bruises appearing as HP percentage drops. Lost hit points are restored by healing or resting.

entries.name: Experience
entries.description: Experience (commonly abbreviated exp. or xp) is a unit of measurement used to quantify the progression of player characters and their companions through the game.

entries.name: Point Buy
entries.description:
Point Buy is the method used by Baldur's Gate 3 to determine a character's Ability Scores during Character Creation. 
The rules of Point Buy when assigning Ability Scores are:

entries.name: Proficiency
entries.description:
Proficiency is a representation of a creature's familiarity with something. When a creature has proficiency in something, they may add their proficiency bonus to dice rolls that involve it.
A creature can have proficiency in specific categories of weapons, armours, and shields, which is required to use them properly. 
A creature can also also have proficiency in spellcasting, saving throws, and skills, but this is not required to attempt them.
Having the same proficiency twice from two different sources does not provided any added bonus.

entries.name: Resistances
entries.description: Resistances represent a creature's capacity to withstand certain types of damage.

entries.name: Character creation
entries.description: When the player starts a new game, they are presented with the character creation screen, where they can either select an origin character, or create a custom one.

entries.name: Classes
entries.description:
A character's class in Baldur's Gate 3 is one of their primary defining features. Each class represents a different calling, and each offers a number of unique abilities, powers, and skills which influence how that character interacts with the world. Classes determine most of a character's abilities - both in and out of combat. As a character advances in levels in a class they gain remarkable new powers and abilities. 
The maximum character level in Baldur's Gate 3 is level 12.
Each class grants characters special dialogue choices only available to that class. Each class also has unique spellcasting animations (while attack animations are based on race).

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries.description:
Backgrounds are a trait which describes a character's life outside of their career as an adventurer. Each background grants characters two skill proficiencies and determines what inspires them. Backgrounds also have narrative effects, including options in dialogue and the opinions or attitude of others towards the character.
Each origin character, including the Dark Urge, has a pre-selected background that cannot be changed. Custom characters select a background on character creation. A character may only have one background, and it cannot be changed once the game is started.

entries.name: Acolyte
entries.description: Acolyte is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around religion. Shadowheart and the hireling Zenith Feur'sel have this background.

entries.name: Charlatan
entries.description: Charlatan is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around trickery and deceit. Astarion and the hireling Kree Derryck have this background.

entries.name: Criminal
entries.description: Criminal is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around law-breaking and the criminal underworld. The hireling Ver'yll Wenkiir has this background.

entries.name: Entertainer
entries.description: Entertainer is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around bardic performances. The hireling Brinna Brightsong has this background.

entries.name: Folk Hero
entries.description: Folk Hero is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around rescuing others from peril. Wyll, Minsc, and the hireling Danton have this background.

entries.name: Guild Artisan
entries.description: Guild Artisan is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around crafting and mercantilism. The hireling Jacelyn has this background.

entries.name: Haunted One
entries.description: Haunted One is a character background unique to the Dark Urge with inspirations themed around embracing (or sometimes resisting) The Urge.

entries.name: Noble
entries.description: Noble is a character background. Minthara and the hireling Kerz have this background.

entries.name: Outlander
entries.description: Outlander is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around exploration and navigating the wilds. Karlach, Halsin, and the hirelings Eldra Luthrinn and Sina'zith have this background.

entries.name: Sage
entries.description: Sage is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around the pursuit of scholarly knowledge. Gale and the hireling Sir Fuzzalump have this background.

entries.name: Soldier
entries.description: Soldier is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around war and masterful combat. Lae'zel, Jaheira, and the hireling Varanna Sunblossom have this background.

entries.name: Urchin
entries.description: Urchin is a character background with skills and inspirations themed around street smarts. The hireling Maddala Deadeye has this background.

entries.name: Races
entries.description:
A creature's race determines its lineage, and innate powers and abilities. Each race has its own strengths, and many possess unique abilities and powers. Sometimes creatures can even cast spells as a result of their racial heritage. Race affects NPC reactions and available interactions during conversations. Each race also has unique attack animations (while spellcasting animations are based on class).
There are several playable and non-playable races of characters and creatures in Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Dragonborn
entries.description: Dragonborn are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3. They have resistance to a type of energy damage, and are able to make deadly breath weapon attacks. These abilities are affected by their dragonborn subrace. Dragonborn resemble draconic humanoids, can have scales in a variety of colours, and may or may not have a tail.

entries.name: Drow
entries.description: Drow are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3. They are the dark elves of the Forgotten Realms, dwelling in the Underdark, large subterranean caverns beneath the surface.

entries.name: Dwarf
entries.description: Dwarves are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Elf
entries.description: Elves are a playable race. They are long lived, and have an affinity for magic.

entries.name: Githyanki
entries.description: Githyanki are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Gnome
entries.description: Gnomes are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Half-Orc
entries.description: Half-orcs are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3. They are born of both human and orc ancestry, and exhibit a blend of orcish and human characteristics, their appearances varying widely.

entries.name: Halfling
entries.description: Halflings are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3.

entries.name: Human
entries.description: Humans are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3. They are one of the most populous races in Faerûn, exhibiting a versatile range of skills rather than any one mastery.

entries.name: Tiefling
entries.description: Tieflings are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3. Touched by the Hells, tieflings are resistant to fire and carry extraordinary Infernal powers.

entries.name: Deities
entries.description: In Forgotten Realms, deities are worshiped by almost everyone, from regular characters to monsters.

entries.name: Corellon Larethian
entries.description: Corellon Larethian is the elven God of art and magic, chaotic good. He is associated with the domains Arcana, Life, Light, War.

entries.name: Eilistraee
entries.description: Eilistraee is the drow goddess of beauty and freedom, chaotic good. She is associated with the domains Life, Light, and Nature.

entries.name: Helm (deity)
entries.description: Helm is the god of protection and guardians, lawful neutral. He is associated with the domains Life, Light, Twilight.

entries.name: Ilmater
entries.description: Ilmater is the god of endurance and suffering. He is associated with the domains Life and Twilight.

entries.name: Lathander
entries.description: Lathander, also known as the Morninglord, is the God of birth, dawn and renewal, neutral good. He is associated with the domains of Life and Light.

entries.name: Lolth
entries.description: Lolth, also known as the Queen of Spiders, is the most influential goddess of the Drow, being the leader of the  Dark Seldarine pantheon.

entries.name: Mystra
entries.description: Mystra is the goddess of magic. She is associated with the domains of Arcana and Knowledge. Player character clerics have the option to select Mystra as their patron deity.

entries.name: Selûne
entries.description: Selûne, also known as The Lady of Silver and the Moonmaiden, is the Goddess of the moon. She is associated with the domains of Knowledge and Life.

entries.name: Tyr
entries.description: Tyr, also known as the Blind God and Maimed God, is the god of law and justice.

entries.name: Vlaakith
entries.description: Vlaakith CLVII is the current and undying ruler of the Githyanki. She oversees their operations in all the planes, and at the time of the events of Baldur's Gate 3, is actively seeking the Mysterious Artefact that was stolen from her. She can also be chosen as a patron deity by githyanki clerics.
